title: September 2019 Class College Final Exam (Part 2 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Medical-Surgical, Paediatrics, Midwifery, Community Health, Mental Health, Pharmacology, Research, Leadership and Management)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 18 November 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q21 to Q40).

questions.text: The second line treatment for uncomplicated malaria is:
questions.explanation: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (C) is correct because Kenya's national malaria treatment policy uses artemether-lumefantrine as first-line and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHA-PPQ) as second-line for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, for example after treatment failure or when AL cannot be used. It is taken on an empty stomach. Quinine (A) is incorrect because it is used for uncomplicated malaria in the first trimester of pregnancy and as an alternative, not as the standard second-line. Artemether-lumefantrine (B) is incorrect because it is the first-line drug. Artesunate (D) is incorrect because IV or IM artesunate is the drug of choice for severe malaria.

questions.text: Protease inhibitors include:
questions.explanation: Ritonavir, Lopinavir (C) is correct because these end in '-navir' and block the HIV protease enzyme, which cuts viral polyproteins into functional proteins; lopinavir is boosted with ritonavir (LPV/r) and is used mainly in second-line regimens. Tenofovir, Lamivudine (A) is incorrect because they are nucleoside/nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs). Nevirapine, Efavirenz (B) is incorrect because they are non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). Dolutegravir, Raltegravir (D) is incorrect because they are integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs), and dolutegravir is the preferred first-line anchor drug in Kenya.

questions.text: The drug of choice for an acute gout attack:
questions.explanation: Colchicine (A) is the marked answer because it relieves the acute inflammation by inhibiting neutrophil migration into the joint and works best when started within 24 hours of the attack (diarrhoea is its commonest side effect); NSAIDs such as indomethacin are an equally accepted first-line alternative. Allopurinol (B) is incorrect because it is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor that lowers uric acid for long-term prevention and can worsen an acute attack if started during it. Sulfinpyrazone (C) is incorrect because it is a uricosuric used in chronic gout. Probenicid (D) is incorrect because it is also a uricosuric for chronic gout and does not treat acute pain.

questions.text: Aspirin prolongs bleeding time by inhibiting the synthesis of:
questions.explanation: Thromboxane A2 in platelets (D) is correct because aspirin irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) in platelets, so thromboxane A2, which causes platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction, is not made; platelets cannot make new enzyme, so the effect lasts for the platelet lifespan of 7 to 10 days and bleeding time is prolonged. Clotting factors in the liver (A) is incorrect because that is the action of warfarin (vitamin K antagonist). Prostacyclin in vascular endothelium (B) is incorrect because prostacyclin prevents platelet aggregation, so lowering it would not prolong bleeding. Cyclic AMP in platelets (C) is incorrect because it is not the mechanism of aspirin; raised cAMP inhibits platelet aggregation.

questions.text: Atorvastatin acts by:

options.A: Decreasing cholesterol synthesis in the liver
options.B: Binding bile acids in the intestines
options.C: Decreasing oxidation of fatty acids in the liver
options.D: Inhibiting absorption of cholesterol in the small intestines

questions.explanation: Decreasing cholesterol synthesis in the liver (A) is correct because atorvastatin inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis, which lowers LDL cholesterol; it is best taken in the evening, and the nurse monitors for muscle pain (myopathy) and liver enzyme changes. Binding bile acids in the intestines (B) is incorrect because it describes bile acid sequestrants such as cholestyramine. Decreasing oxidation of fatty acids in the liver (C) is incorrect because it is not a statin action; fibrates increase fatty acid oxidation. Inhibiting absorption of cholesterol in the small intestines (D) is incorrect because it describes ezetimibe.

questions.text: Mr. Z, 40 years old displays unusual rigidity, orderliness and punctuality. According to Freud as a child Mr. Z experienced:
questions.explanation: Strict toilet training (B) is correct because in Freud's psychosexual theory, harsh or overly strict toilet training during the anal stage (about 1 to 3 years) leads to an anal-retentive personality, marked by rigidity, orderliness, punctuality, stubbornness and stinginess. Timed breastfeeding schedule (A) is incorrect because feeding experiences belong to the oral stage and lead to oral traits such as dependency, smoking or over-eating. Poor bonding with the mother (C) is incorrect because it is linked to attachment and trust problems (Erikson, Bowlby) rather than the anal fixation described. Good interactions with peers (D) is incorrect because peer relationships belong to the latency stage and are healthy development.

questions.text: Student Q prepares adequately to avoid failing examination. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement (B) is correct because in operant conditioning a behaviour (preparing well) is strengthened by removing or avoiding an unpleasant outcome (failing the exam). Positive reinforcement (A) is incorrect because it strengthens behaviour by adding something pleasant, such as praise or a reward. Positive punishment (C) is incorrect because it reduces a behaviour by adding something unpleasant, such as a reprimand. Negative punishment (D) is incorrect because it reduces a behaviour by taking away something pleasant, such as losing privileges.

questions.text: Health messages for a patient with myasthenia gravis on prevention of myasthenic and cholinergic crisis include:

options.C: Doing all chores early in the day while less fatigued

questions.explanation: Taking medications on time (D) is correct because the anticholinesterase drugs (for example pyridostigmine) must be taken exactly as prescribed: late or missed doses allow weakness to build up into a myasthenic crisis, while extra doses cause excess acetylcholine and a cholinergic crisis. Eating a balanced meal (A) is incorrect as the best answer because it supports general health, though meals are timed to medication for chewing and swallowing. Performing muscle strengthening exercises (B) is incorrect because exertion worsens muscle fatigue in myasthenia. Doing all chores early in the day while less fatigued (C) is incorrect because energy is conserved by spacing activities with rest periods, not by doing all chores at once.

questions.text: The nurse assesses oculovestibular reflex by:

options.A: Turning the patient's head suddenly while holding the eyelids open
options.B: Introducing cold water into the external auditory canal
options.C: Shining a bright light into the eye
options.D: Touching the cornea with a wisp of cotton

questions.explanation: Introducing cold water into the external auditory canal (B) is correct because the oculovestibular (cold caloric) reflex is tested by irrigating the ear with ice-cold water after confirming an intact eardrum, with the head raised to 30 degrees; an intact brainstem makes the eyes deviate toward the irrigated ear. Turning the patient's head suddenly while holding the eyelids open (A) is incorrect because it describes the oculocephalic (doll's eye) reflex, which must not be done if there is a suspected cervical spine injury. Shining a bright light into the eye (C) is incorrect because it tests the pupillary light reflex (cranial nerves II and III). Touching the cornea with a wisp of cotton (D) is incorrect because it tests the corneal reflex (cranial nerves V and VII).

questions.text: The purpose of pulmonary function test is to:

options.B: Determine oxygen and carbon dioxide concentration
options.C: Measure the lung volumes and capacity
options.D: Measure the gas diffusion rate at the alveolar capillary membrane

questions.explanation: Measure the lung volumes and capacity (C) is correct because pulmonary function tests (spirometry) measure ventilation, such as tidal volume, FVC, FEV1 and total lung capacity, and are used to tell obstructive from restrictive lung disease and to follow progress of asthma and COPD. Evaluate pulmonary causes of hypoxia (A) is incorrect because hypoxia is assessed with pulse oximetry and arterial blood gases. Determine oxygen and carbon dioxide concentration (B) is incorrect because that is done by arterial blood gas analysis. Measure the gas diffusion rate at the alveolar capillary membrane (D) is incorrect because it describes only the diffusing capacity test (DLCO), one component of a full study, not the main purpose.

questions.text: On percussion hyper-resonant sound is associated with:
questions.explanation: Emphysema (D) is correct because destruction of alveolar walls and air trapping make the chest hyperinflated and full of air, which gives a hyper-resonant (booming) percussion note, as does a pneumothorax. Atelectasis (A) is incorrect because collapsed airless lung gives a dull note. Lung cancer (B) is incorrect because a solid tumour mass gives dullness. Lung abscess (C) is incorrect because a pus-filled, consolidated area gives dullness.

questions.text: An immunoglobulin that contributes to the pathophysiologic characteristics of asthma is:
questions.explanation: IgE (C) is correct because in allergic asthma the allergen triggers production of IgE, which attaches to mast cells; on re-exposure the mast cells release histamine and leukotrienes, causing bronchoconstriction, mucosal oedema and mucus secretion. IgA (A) is incorrect because it protects mucosal surfaces such as saliva, tears and the gut. IgG (B) is incorrect because it is the main antibody of secondary immune response and the only one that crosses the placenta. IgM (D) is incorrect because it is the first antibody produced in primary infection.

questions.text: A patient diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on two liters of oxygen, has a respiratory rate of 28br/min. the action that the nurse should take is:

options.A: Determine the need to increase the oxygen
options.B: Reassure the patient that there is no need to worry

questions.explanation: Determine the need to increase the oxygen (A) is the marked answer because a respiratory rate of 28 per minute shows respiratory distress, so the nurse first assesses the patient (oxygen saturation, work of breathing, colour, mental state, blood gases) to decide whether oxygen needs adjusting; in COPD any increase is made carefully, usually titrated to a saturation of about 88 to 92%, because too much oxygen can blunt the hypoxic drive and cause carbon dioxide retention. Reassure the patient that there is no need to worry (B) is incorrect because it ignores a worsening sign. Administer bronchodilators (C) is incorrect as the first action because they need a prescription and assessment first. Perform a chest physiotherapy (D) is incorrect because it can tire an already distressed patient.

questions.text: In nursing ethics, Veracity means:
questions.explanation: Telling the truth (D) is correct because veracity is the duty to be truthful and honest with patients and not to deceive them, which supports informed consent and trust. Doing good (A) is incorrect because it is beneficence. Doing no harm (B) is incorrect because it is non-maleficence. Being fair (C) is incorrect because it is justice.

questions.text: A function of National nurses' association of Kenya is:

options.A: Ensuring circulation of information by journals bulletins and newsletters
options.B: Prescribing and regulating syllabuses of instruction
options.C: Conducting examinations for persons seeking registration
options.D: Inspecting and approving institutions for training nurses

questions.explanation: Ensuring circulation of information by journals bulletins and newsletters (A) is correct because the National Nurses Association of Kenya (NNAK) is the professional association that looks after the welfare of nurses, promotes professional development and keeps members informed through publications. Prescribing and regulating syllabuses of instruction (B) is incorrect because that is a function of the Nursing Council of Kenya (NCK). Conducting examinations for persons seeking registration (C) is incorrect because the NCK conducts the licensing and registration examinations. Inspecting and approving institutions for training nurses (D) is incorrect because the NCK also inspects and accredits nurse training institutions.

questions.text: The crude death rate is the number of deaths in a population in a given year per:
questions.explanation: 1000-member population (B) is correct because the crude death rate is the total number of deaths in a year divided by the mid-year population, multiplied by 1,000. It is called crude because it does not adjust for age or sex. 100-member population (A) is incorrect because it would be a percentage. 10,000-member population (C) is incorrect because that base is not used for the crude death rate. 100,000-member population (D) is incorrect because that base is used for rarer events such as cause-specific mortality and the maternal mortality ratio.

questions.text: Nurse GG is performing limb observation and she instructs the patient to close their eyes. The nurse is evaluating the patient's:
questions.explanation: Paresthesia (C) is correct because in a neurovascular limb check the patient closes the eyes while the nurse lightly touches the limb, so that the patient reports sensation (numbness, tingling, pins and needles, or loss of feeling) without being helped by sight. Pain (A) is incorrect because it is assessed by asking the patient to describe and score it. Paralysis (B) is incorrect because it is assessed by asking the patient to move the limb with eyes open and checking muscle power. Pallor (D) is incorrect because it is assessed by looking at the skin colour and temperature, which does not need the patient's eyes closed.

questions.text: An internal risk factor for pressure sore development is:
questions.explanation: Previous history of bed sore (B) is correct because internal (intrinsic) risk factors are those within the patient, such as old age, poor nutrition, immobility, incontinence, diabetes, poor circulation and a previous pressure ulcer, since healed skin is weaker and more likely to break down again. Duration of pressure (A) is incorrect because it is an external (extrinsic) factor, together with friction, shear and moisture. Type of mattress in use (C) is incorrect because it is an external factor from the environment. Level of nursing care available (D) is incorrect because it is a health-system factor outside the patient.

questions.text: An example of a lymphatic tissue nematode is:
questions.explanation: Brugia malayi (D) is correct because the lymphatic filarial worms are Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi and Brugia timori, whose adults live in lymph vessels and nodes and cause lymphoedema and elephantiasis. Loa loa (A) is incorrect because it lives in subcutaneous tissue and can cross the eye (eye worm, Calabar swellings). Onchocerca volvulus (B) is incorrect because it forms nodules in the skin and causes river blindness. Dracunculus medinensis (C) is incorrect because the guinea worm lives in subcutaneous tissue and emerges through a skin ulcer.

questions.text: Nocturnal periodicity is witnessed in:
questions.explanation: Wuchereria bancrofti (A) is correct because its microfilariae appear in the peripheral blood mostly at night (about 10 pm to 2 am), matching the biting time of the Culex and Anopheles mosquito vectors, so blood for the film should be taken at night. Dracunculus medinensis (B) is incorrect because it has no microfilariae in the blood; the female releases larvae into water. Trichuris trichiura (C) is incorrect because it is an intestinal whipworm diagnosed by eggs in stool. Strongyloides stercoralis (D) is incorrect because its larvae are found in stool and it shows no blood periodicity.
